analysis.summary: BffApi route function names are ignored by enrichRoutes, causing potential AWS Lambda naming collisions across feature apps

bugs.title: Function name override causes resource collisions
bugs.description: Route definitions provide custom functionName including featureAppName for uniqueness, but enrichRoutes generates its own functionName without featureAppName, ignoring the provided value. This causes all feature apps to attempt creating Lambda functions with identical names (e.g., 'BFF-PRODUCTION-GET-app-model-prod'), leading to deployment failures or cross-app resource overwrites.
bugs.risk: HIGH: AWS Lambda function names must be unique within a region. When multiple feature apps deploy, they will collide on function names causing CloudFormation deployment failures or one app overwriting another's functions.

notBugs.reason: The URL path stripping logic was removed from CloudFront because the webpack output path was updated to include the full __app__/featureAppName/target prefix, making S3 object keys match the incoming request paths exactly. The .html appending logic removal appears intentional as part of the BFF standardization architecture change.

The pathRewrite removal is correct and consistent with the BffApi.ts changes. The BFF routes now include the full baseUrl path (/__app__/.../bff/...), so the proxy must forward the full path rather than stripping the prefix.

The enrichRoutes function destructures only handler, timeout, and memorySize. While it ignores the new functionName property, this does not cause a runtime error by itself (destructuring ignores extra properties), though it does create the logical bug described above.
